source_caption:
“Spider-Man: No Way Home” was one of the greatest comic book movie experiences ever! 🕷️

For years, fans had dreamed about seeing Tobey Maguire, Andrew Garfield, and Tom Holland together in one Spider-Man movie. Somehow, Marvel and Sony actually made it happen.

Even Tom Holland didn’t think it would work at first. When director Jon Watts pitched him the idea of bringing the three Spider-Men together, Holland thought there was no way they would all agree. But eventually, all three actors came on board. 

The secrecy around it was also insane.

Andrew Garfield spent years denying that he was in the movie. He even had to lie to Emma Stone, his former Amazing Spider-Man co-star, when she asked him about it. He later revealed that only a few people close to him knew he was filming the movie.

And when the three finally put on their Spider-Man suits together, Holland said they spent their first day swapping stories about the costumes — including how to get into them and where all the zippers were. Imagine being in that room. 

There was also a beautiful moment for Garfield and Maguire after the movie came out. The two secretly went to a packed opening-night screening together, wearing baseball caps and masks so they could watch the audience experience the movie without being recognized.

And the audience reaction was enormous.

Released in December 2021, No Way Home opened to $260 million domestically and eventually made more than $1.9 billion worldwide. It became one of the biggest box-office hits ever and the highest-grossing Spider-Man movie at the time.

But the numbers only tell part of the story.

For an entire generation of fans, seeing three different versions of Spider-Man standing together on the big screen wasn’t just another crossover.

It was the moment three eras of Spider-Man finally became one.

source_details.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
source_details.synopsis: Spider-Man: No Way Home is a 2021 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man. Produced by Columbia Pictures, Marvel Studios, and Pascal Pictures, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing, it is the sequel to Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017) and Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019), and the 27th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU). The film was directed by Jon Watts, written by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, and stars Tom Holland as Peter Parker / Spider-Man alongside Zendaya, Benedict Cumberbatch, Jacob Batalon, Jon Favreau, Jamie Foxx, Willem Dafoe, Alfred Molina, Benedict Wong, Tony Revolori, Marisa Tomei, Andrew Garfield, and Tobey Maguire.
